html:
At midnight on 30 June 1997 Britain handed Hong Kong to the People's Republic of China, in a ceremony at the convention centre on Victoria Harbour, ending 156 years of British rule.

The last governor, Chris Patten, sailed away on the royal yacht Britannia with the Prince of Wales. Chinese troops crossed the border, and the shipping magnate Tung Chee-hwa became the first chief executive of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, under the terms of the Joint Declaration.

For many it marked the end of the British Empire, begun in this region with the seizure of the island in 1841. Days later the Asian financial crisis struck. Two years later Macau followed. Life went on much as before for a decade, until fights over democracy grew.
sum: At midnight on 30 June 1997 Britain handed Hong Kong to the People's Republic of China, in a ceremony at the convention centre on Victoria Harbour, ending 156 years of British rule.
